answer: A courier-agent registry uses a wander test: 5 sequential deliveries of sealed onyx parcels from a registered forge to randomly chosen depots. Each depot signs the agent key, parcel ID and arrival time; the next pickup is allowed only after that receipt. Admission requires all 5 receipts, and parcel IDs cannot count for another key. Each extra alias needs its own completed deliveries, imposing transport costs rather than merely new keys. Colluding depots could fabricate receipts; independent spot audits are needed.
